title: top-io.json — the module's top-level IO ports (authored, never derived)
description: The DUT boundary. derive-constraints renders create_clock / set_input_delay / set_output_delay / abstract_port from it; simulation-plan derives agents and transaction fields from it; each rtl-design child reads it for set_case_analysis. A reset row also declares polarity and kind.

name.description: The port name exactly as the netlist declares it, bit range included (e.g. token_in[4:0]). Emitted verbatim into get_ports / abstract_port, so it is not decomposed here.

width.description: Bit width. When name ends in a [h:l] range, the two must agree — cross-checked when this file is read; an [i] index (a register-file element) carries no width claim and is skipped.

clock_domain.description: A clocks.json name. Clock and reset ports carry no IO delay; each data port gets set_input/output_delay against this domain.

interface_group.description: Groups ports into one TB agent / one vif.

encoding.description: A control or status port pins its bit/field-to-symbol meaning here: single-bit as "0:<meaning>; 1:<meaning>", multi-bit per field as "bit[h:l] <name>: <code>:<symbol>; …". For a phase or command code write the CONSUMER OBLIGATION, not just a label — e.g. "3:PV (consumer re-preloads the stationary operand, then streams)". This entry is the single source: a child names the port and never re-describes the codes. Raw data / clock / reset ports have none. Enforced by the spec-review conformance lens, not by a deterministic gate.
